brief.text:
SITUATION NOW
Thousands protested in Madrid against the housing crisis, and an elderly woman's eviction has put Spain's housing crisis in the spotlight. [2][5]

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR SPAIN
The housing protests in Madrid underscore public frustration that could increase political pressure, especially as a market gives a 79% probability that Alberto Núñez Feijóo will be the next Prime Minister. [5][E6]
Spain's 69% net energy import dependency makes the Strait of Gibraltar shipping chokepoint critical for its energy security, a vulnerability highlighted by the ongoing housing crisis. [2][E3][E4]

KEY RISKS
Spain's 69% net energy import dependency exposes it to supply disruptions, particularly through the Strait of Gibraltar chokepoint. [E3][E4]
Spain is linked to 52 US OFAC and Canada SEMA sanctions designations, posing compliance and reputational risks. [E2]

OUTLOOK
A Polymarket market on Alberto Núñez Feijóo becoming the next Prime Minister is priced Yes at 79% as of Sep 28, 2026, and closes Apr 1, 2028. [E6]

WATCH ITEMS
It is unresolved whether the housing protests in Madrid will lead to policy changes or further escalation. [5]
